summary: Palladium and ruthenium were deposited on alumina and silica supports using atomic layer deposition (ALE) with Pd(thd)2 and Ru(thd)3 as precursors. The study focused on the reduction of these complexes to metallic palladium and ruthenium, and the interaction mechanisms with the oxide supports. The reduction temperatures were determined based on TGA data, and the results showed that the ALE process led to smaller crystallite sizes compared to impregnation.
evidence: Palladium and ruthenium were deposited on alumina and silica supports from gas phase by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and from liquid phase by impregnation with use of /H9252-diketonate complexes as precursors. The reduction temperatures were determined based on TGA data. The ALE samples showed smaller crystallite sizes compared to impregnated samples.
